subject: Round 1 data processing addendum — cross-border transfers & subprocessor transparency
messages:
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@startsafe.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@startsafe.com>
Date: 2028-02-18T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Initial round of DPA comments and subprocessor ask

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

Thanks for sending over the base data processing addendum. Amanda and I reviewed and put together a first-pass redline (attached). High level items we want to discuss:

- Cross-border transfers: we need to confirm whether Redwood relies on SCCs, a UK addendum, or an EU–US transfer mechanism. The redline suggests a combined approach; we'd prefer explicit reference to the SCCs plus an attestation of any UK addendum coverage.
- Subprocessors: please include a current subprocessor list and your notification cadence (30 days vs 60 days). We flagged the clause to require 30 days' notice for new subprocessors with an opt-out right for StartSafe.
- Security attachments: we asked for the SOC 2 scope and whether logs/audit artifacts are retained for 12 months.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the technical answers? If possible, we'd like to have a quick call on Monday to walk through the redline and path to execution (DocuSign preferred).

Thanks,
Liam
Legal — StartSafe Inc.
attachments: StartSafe_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (docx)

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@startsafe.com>, Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@startsafe.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-18T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Initial round of DPA comments and subprocessor ask

Hi Liam / Amanda — great to meet you virtually.

Thanks for the redline. Quick answers up front:
- Transfers: Redwood's default is SCCs + EU–UK addendum where applicable. We can provide a short attestation statement to include in the addendum.
- Subprocessors: we maintain an internal register; we can export the live list (see attached redwood_subprocessors_2028Q1.xlsx). Our standard notice is 30 days for new subprocessors and we do provide an opt-out right for certain regulated customers — we'll confirm the specific language.
- SOC 2: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report covers the serving runtime and control plane; logs are retained for 12 months by default. We can provide a scope summary.

Neha, would you and Dev please review the redline and confirm the technical bits (SCCs/attestation language, log retention) so I can get back to Liam with a suggested counter?

I'm available for a 30-minute call Monday 10:00–11:00 ET or Tuesday afternoon. If that works for you, we'll send a calendar invite and aim to route the agreed form via DocuSign.

— Tessa
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_subprocessors_2028Q1.xlsx (xlsx)

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-18T14:27:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Initial round of DPA comments and subprocessor ask

Tessa — quick technical confirmations after reviewing attachments:

- Transfer mechanism: Confirmed — we rely on the EU SCCs (post-2021 template) and we have a UK addendum available. I will draft a one-paragraph attestation that we can insert in the addendum: "Redwood Inference processes Customer Personal Data under the EU SCCs and provides a UK Addendum where applicable."
- Logs & retention: Audit logs and request traces are retained 12 months. For enterprise customers we offer extended retention as an add-on; include a note in the DPA that retention can be extended by written agreement.
- Subprocessor cadence: The exported sheet reflects live subprocessors. For sensitive customers we offer an expedited notice and a 14-day review window for critical subprocessors, but the standard is 30 days.

I'll prepare suggested counter-language for the redline and propose insert locations for the attestation and retention options.

Neha
Product & Privacy

From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@startsafe.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@startsafe.com>
Date: 2028-02-20T09:05:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Initial round of DPA comments and subprocessor ask

Thanks — that helps. Two follow ups from our counsel:

1) Liability cap carve-out for data breaches: StartSafe is asking for a limited carve-out from the general cap if there is a regulated data subject harm or a GDPR enforcement fine directly caused by Redwood's failure to comply. They asked for example language; can Redwood provide a suggested approach that balances your commercial cap with StartSafe's regulatory risk?

2) DocuSign execution: counsel requested that the executed document show the full redline history and be signed by an authorized signatory with title. We plan to run this via our e-sign environment.

Would appreciate a proposed counter on the carve-out and confirmation we can execute in DocuSign (we can pre-seed the envelope if you confirm your signer).

– Liam

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@startsafe.com>, Amanda Lee <amanda.lee@startsafe.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-21T16:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Initial round of DPA comments and subprocessor ask

Liam — thanks, appreciate the clarity.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Neha will send a concise counter-proposal addressing: (a) an attestation sentence for SCCs/UK addendum; (b) sample liability carve-out language that limits exposure but acknowledges regulatory fines where permitted by law.
2) Dev to confirm the signatory name and title: Redwood's authorized sig is Alex Grant, VP, Legal & Ops. We will accept DocuSign and can either (a) receive an envelope from StartSafe or (b) create the envelope and route to you first. Please indicate your preference.
3) We'll aim to consolidate the counter redline in one tracked document and return within 48 hours.

If that approach works, we'll set DocuSign routing and target execution following legal sign-off.

Best,
Tessa
